en.title: Slovenia: 53 cm snow forecast for next week, peak on 26 November
en.description: Slovenia faces major snowfall over the next 7 days, with up to 53 cm expected. The heaviest falls arrive on 26 November. Data from 21 November.
en.lede: Slovenia will receive up to 53 cm of new snow in the next seven days, with the snowiest day on 26 November bringing 25 cm. This week's storm will add significant water to the mountains, raising the snow line and rebuilding cover after recent melt.

sections.h: What the next seven days will bring
p: A major snow system is moving toward Slovenia's mountains. Between now and 28 November, the high-altitude areas will gain up to 53 cm. The forecast shows most of this snow will arrive between now and 26 November, with 25 cm falling on that single day. This concentrated event means rapid water input to the mountain snowpack.

The 72-hour period just ended (18-21 November) already left 28 cm in the Julian Alps and 44 cm in the Kamnik-Savinja Alps. That sequence has stabilised conditions at higher elevations. The coming system will push the snow line higher and fill gaps left by recent warm days.

Sella Nevea sits highest at 2,137 m and already holds 28 cm from recent storms. It will receive up to 22 cm more in the next three days, keeping it as the main snow reservoir. Krvavec at 1,963 m will also benefit, gaining 23 cm over three days to reach a usable depth.

Above 2,000 m across the region, snow cover is now complete (100 percent). Between 1,500 and 2,000 m, cover stands at 83 percent, with a mean depth of 7 cm. The incoming snow will push reliable cover down to around 1,500 m by week's end, where water storage matters most for winter runoff.

sections.h: Snow depth now and the week ahead
p: Measured snow on the ground today covers 750 km2 across the modelled area, down 40 km2 from yesterday but stable after yesterday's slow melt. This total is still well below the 1,160 km2 recorded seven days ago, before the warm spell. The incoming snow will reverse that trend sharply.

In the three days after 26 November (27-29 November), falls will ease to a maximum of 18 cm. Week two (29 November to 5 December) looks drier, with only 15 cm possible. This pattern means the main water input arrives in the next 5 to 6 days, then slows.

The snow line now sits at 1,500 m. Above that, conditions are locked in: mean depth 7 cm from 1,500 to 2,000 m, and 20 cm from 2,000 to 2,500 m. Below 1,500 m, little snow persists (1 cm mean depth between 1,000 and 1,500 m; almost none below 1,000 m).

When 25 cm falls on 26 November, highest zones will reach 30-45 cm, depending on aspect and terrain. The 1,500 to 2,000 m band—critical for water storage—will gain most of the new snow and climb rapidly toward 30 cm. This is where winter water reserves build.

The past five days saw sharp swings. Snow cover dropped from 1,130 km2 (16 November) to just 260 km2 (18 November) as warm air melted lower slopes. Fresh snowfall on 19 November pushed it back to 760 km2. Today's figure of 750 km2 shows minor further loss, but the arrival of heavier snow will arrest that decline.

Sella Nevea has led throughout, holding 28 cm today. Soriška planina and Golte received little fresh snow (1-4 cm in 72 hours) and sit lower in terms of depth and elevation, so they will gain snow more slowly as the system progresses.

sections.h: Nearby context: Austria and Italy ahead
p: Austria's high glaciated peaks already hold 63 cm (Stubaier Gletscher) and face up to 35 cm more in seven days. Italy's leading site, Pfelders, sits at 118 cm—far deeper than Slovenia. These neighbours show what well-established winter snowpack looks like; Slovenia is still building toward that standard. The coming week is a critical step in that direction.

advice: Expect rapid snow depth increase between now and 27 November, especially above 1,500 m where most water will be stored. Travel high to find the thickest new snow.
On 26 November, the heaviest falls will arrive. Plan mountain activities for clear windows on 22-25 November if stability is a concern; fresh snow always carries temporary instability risk.
Below 1,500 m, snow cover remains patchy. Early-season rocks and thin patches are likely; check actual conditions carefully on lower slopes until cover thickens.

By late November, water input to streams and reservoirs will spike as melt accelerates from warm base layers beneath new snow. Monitor local water management updates if you work with mountain hydrology.
Consult the official avalanche bulletin (ARSO) before any off-piste activity, particularly on steep slopes receiving fresh snow between 1,500 and 2,000 m.

sl.title: Slovenija: 53 cm snega napovedano za naslednjo teden, vrhunec 26. novembra
sl.description: Slovenijo čaka obsežna snežna padavina v naslednjih 7 dneh, pričakuje se do 53 cm snega. Največje padavine prihajajo 26. novembra. Podatki od 21. novembra.
sl.lede: Slovenija bo v naslednjih sedmih dneh prejela do 53 cm novega snega, s snežnim vrhuncem 26. novembra, ko bo padlo 25 cm. Viharjenja tega tedna bo dodalo pomembno količino vode v gore, zvišalo snežno mejo in obnovilo snežno odejo po nedavnem taljenju.

sections.h: Kaj nas čaka v naslednjih sedmih dneh
p: Proti slovenskim gorам se pomika obsežen snežni sistem. Med zdajšnjim časom in 28. novembrom bodo visoke nadmorske višine prejele do 53 cm snega. Napoved kaže, da bo večina tega snega padla med zdajšnjim časom in 26. novembrom, pri čemer bo 25 cm padlo v enem samem dnevu. Ta koncentrirani dogodek pomeni hitro dovajanje vode v gorski snežni pokrov.

Tridnevno obdobje, ki se je pravkar končalo (18.–21. november), je v Julijcih pustilo 28 cm in 44 cm v Kamniško-Savinjskih Alpah. To zaporedje je stabiliziralo razmere na večjih nadmorskih višinah. Prihajajući sistem bo dvignil snežno mejo in zapolnil vrzeli, ki jih je pustilo nedavno toplo obdobje.

Sella Nevea je na največji nadmorski višini 2.137 m in že ima 28 cm snega iz nedavnih viharjev. V naslednjih treh dneh bo prejela do 22 cm več, saj bo ohranjena kot glavna snežna zajetnica. Krvavec na 1.963 m bo prav tako profitiral, saj bo dobil 23 cm v treh dneh in dosegel uporabno globino.

Nad 2.000 m v celotnem območju je snežni pokrov zdaj popoln (100 odstotkov). Med 1.500 in 2.000 m je pokrov 83-odstoten, s povprečno globino 7 cm. Prihajajući sneg bo potisnit zanesljiv pokrov do približno 1.500 m do konca tedna, kjer je shranjevanje vode najpomembnejše za zimski odtok.

sections.h: Globina snega zdaj in v tednu naprej
p: Izmerjeni sneg na tleh danes pokriva 750 km² na modeliranem območju, kar je 40 km² manj kot včeraj, vendar je stabilno po včerajšnjem počasnem taljenju. Ta skupni seštevek je še vedno daleč pod 1.160 km², zabeleženo pred sedmimi dnevi, pred toplim obdobjem. Prihajajući sneg bo ta trend ostro obrnit.

V treh dneh po 26. novembru (27.–29. november) se bodo padavine oslabile na največ 18 cm. Drugi teden (29. november do 5. decembra) izgleda bolj suho, z le 15 cm. Ta razporeditev pomeni, da главни vnos vode prihaja v naslednjih 5 do 6 dni, nato se upočasni.

Snežna meja je zdaj na 1.500 m. Nad to, so razmerja zaklenjena: povprečna globina 7 cm od 1.500 do 2.000 m in 20 cm od 2.000 do 2.500 m. Pod 1.500 m se malo snega obdrži (povprečna globina 1 cm med 1.000 in 1.500 m; skoraj nič pod 1.000 m).

Ko 25 cm pada 26. novembra, bodo najvišje cone dosegla 30–45 cm, odvisno od orientacije in terena. Pas 1.500 do 2.000 m—kritičen za shranjevanje vode—bo dobil večino novega snega in hitro narasel proti 30 cm. Tu se gradijo zimske zaloge vode.

Zadnjih pet dni je videlo ostre nihaje. Snežni pokrov je padel s 1.130 km² (16. november) na vsega 260 km² (18. november), ko je topel zrak stalil nižje nakalone. Svež sneg 19. novembra ga je potisnil nazaj na 760 km². Današnja številka 750 km² kaže še manjšo izgubo, vendar bo prihod težjega snega ta padec ustavil.

Sella Nevea je vodila skozi celoten čas, saj je danes ohranila 28 cm. Soriška planina in Golte sta prejeli malo svežega snega (1–4 cm v 72 urah) in sta nižje v smislu globine in nadmorske višine, zato bosta sneg dobivali počasneje, ko se bo sistem развивati.

sections.h: Bližnji kontekst: Avstrija in Italija naprej
p: Avstrijske visoke ledeniskaste vrhove že držijo 63 cm (Stubaier Gletscher) in se soočajo do 35 cm več v sedmih dneh. Vodioca Italije, Pfelders, je pri 118 cm—mnogo globlji kot Slovenija. Ti sosedje kažejo, kaj dobro vzpostavljen zimski snežni pokrov izgleda; Slovenija še gradi proti temu standardu. Prihajajući teden je kritičen korak v tej smeri.

advice: Pričakujte hitro povečanje globine snega med zdajšnjim časom in 27. novembrom, posebej nad 1.500 m, kjer bo večina vode shranjena. Odpravite se visoko, da najdete najgloblji nov sneg.

26. novembra bodo prispele največje padavine. Načrtujte gorske dejavnosti za jasna vremenska okna med 22. in 25. novembrom, če vas skrbi stabilnost; sveži sneg vedno nosi tveganje začasne nestabilnosti.
Pod 1.500 m ostaja snežni pokrov mozaičen. Zgodnje kamnine in tanka tla so verjetni; pazljivo preverite dejanske razmere na nižjih pobočjih, dokler se pokrov ne zgosti.

Konec novembra bo vnos vode v tokove in zajetnice skokovito skočil, ko se pospešeno taliranje iz toplih baznih plasti pod novim snegom. Sproti spremljajte uradne posodobitve upravljanja vode, če delate s horsko hidrologijo.
Pred vsako dejavnostjo izven teras se posvetujte s to uradnim lavinama plakato (ARSO), posebej na strmih pobočjih, ki prejemajo sveži sneg med 1.500 in 2.000 m.
